page: Microsoft Azure E8pds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture. It is powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a clock frequency of 3.0 GHz. The instance delivers 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Hyper-V serves as the underlying hypervisor. Accelerator hardware is not included, leaving the system with zero GPUs. For local scratch needs, the server bundles 322 GB of local SSD storage alongside support for Premium Storage.

With 64.0 GB of system memory, the instance provides an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, aligning directly with memory-intensive software profiles. Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached read bandwidth of 91.15 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 46.81 GB/sec, placing it in the average tier across tested cloud hardware. While multi-core benchmarks like stress-ng multi-core (14,512.41) and Clang software compilation (8,710.0) demonstrate competent parallel performance, single-threaded metrics show limitations. Geekbench single-core (1,081.0) and PassMark CPU overall (6,226.55) fall into the lower quartile, reflecting the architectural characteristics of Neoverse-N1 cores when processing strictly serial or vector-heavy tasks without AVX extensions.

In operational benchmark tests, the instance executed 10.98 million Redis SET operations per second and handled 10.58 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, both showing mid-range throughput capability. In contrast, CPU-driven LLM inference performs poorly, generating only 7.51 tokens per second on a 7B model. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based CPU architecture delivers high RAM density and predictable dedicated-core compute at a balanced operational footprint. The configuration is best aligned with in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, relational and NoSQL databases, memory-centric microservices, and general data processing tasks requiring high memory-to-core ratios without requiring x86-specific instruction sets.
description: Microsoft Azure E8pds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated arm64 physical cores powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. It includes 64.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 8.0 GB per core allocation, alongside 322 GB of bundled local SSD storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark results place its multi-core compute and memory bandwidth in the mid-range tier, evidenced by 14,512.41 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 10.98 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core execution and CPU-based LLM inference are comparatively weak. Providing dedicated core execution and high memory capacity, the E8pds_v5 offers solid qualitative efficiency for memory-heavy ARM workloads. It is well suited for in-memory key-value databases, medium relational database deployments, backend caching clusters, and memory-intensive enterprise services.
